audit.why: Lane difficulty: Mel bullies the weak pre-6 Vladimir, level 6 is his one lane window, and he outscales into teamfights — EVEN 5.5/10 is defensible.

audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer chart rows 3-4 carry blanket 'Skill' while content win[3]=Mel, win[4]=Vladimir (matching packet). Rows 5-6 disagree across layers (full: Vladimir, content+packet: Mel) and the packet itself flags the chart as contradicting the 43.98% win rate.
audit.why: Rows 3-4 are kit-groundable (Vlad pre-6 can only sustain; Hemoplague+pool at 6 is his window) so I aligned them. Rows 5-6 I cannot adjudicate from the kit — sources split — so I left them per the chart rule.
audit.corrected: phases[3].side->Mel, phases[4].side->Vladimir with matching whys; rows 5-6 untouched, recorded in notes.

audit.whatIsWrong: Content claims Rebuttal 'reflects' Tides of Blood. Tides of Blood is an AoE burst around Vladimir with no projectile flag — nothing to reflect. Rebuttal still prevents the damage while active.
audit.why: Kit: Vlad E has slow+zone flags only; Mel W 'reflects enemy projectiles... prevents her from taking damage'. Transfusion is the reflectable piece. Sanguine Pool (28-16s) is untargetable for 2s and dodges Solar Snare and the R strike.
audit.corrected: 'reflects' changed to 'blocks' in whys[6], spikes[3].text and late; projectile distinction stated in dontsFull[2].d.

audit.why: Trade guidance (root Q animation, punish sustain-only early) matches both kits.
Kit numbers: Sanguine Pool 28/25/22/19/16, Transfusion 9 to 4.6, Mel W 38s rank 1.
Wave text is serviceable and Mel-specific.
Level 6 jungle-assisted all-in warning present in spikes[1].
report[8] already says anti-heal early into his sustain — the missing-interaction is covered there and in the new cooldowns line.

audit.whatIsWrong: enemyWin is the templated 'wins by landing X, denying your pattern' sentence.
audit.corrected: Rewritten around pool dodging the snare, Transfusion sustain, Hemoplague scaling.

audit.why: Mistakes list is specific once the projectile fix lands.
Untargetable-dodges-burst missing interaction already covered (bait pool, then E-lock, execute post-pool).
No patch movement claimed; none verifiable from the brief.

edits.before: Vladimir wins by landing Sanguine Pool, denying your pattern, and renting you the lane at a range markup.
edits.after: Vladimir wins by pooling through your snare, healing your chip with Transfusion, and outscaling into Hemoplague.

edits.before: - Vladimir Sanguine Pool: matchup-defining — Untargetable dodge — bait it before you spend your kill window. Count it out loud if you must. - Your W Rebuttal has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Vladimir Sanguine Pool: 28s at rank 1, 16s max — untargetable dodge; bait it before you spend the kill window. - Transfusion is 9s early and 4.6s max: his sustain accelerates, so anti-heal by mid game. - Your 38s Rebuttal answers Q, not the pool.

edits.before: Q-volley the last-hit, bank the overwhelm stacks, and keep W glowing — the chip is free while his best spells are hostages.
edits.after: Transfusion is 9s at rank 1 — Q his last-hit attempts in that gap; he can only heal it back, never trade into 950 range.

edits.before: Burning Rebuttal on chip and then eating the full rotation it existed to return — the reflect is the matchup; spend it like a verdict.
edits.after: Sanguine Pool and Tides of Blood aren't projectiles — Rebuttal returns Transfusion only, so the glow never stops his all-in burst.

edits.before: Lost Chapter timing — volley every wave contact and bank the overwhelm stacks on his health bar.
edits.after: You still chunk him faster than Transfusion heals and he lacks his all-in — keep the chip going.

edits.before: Golden Eclipse online — the execute threshold turns your chip war into a countdown he can see.
edits.after: Hemoplague plus charged Tides and Q-heal is a real all-in, and the pool dodges your snare at 6.

edits.before: At 2+ items you win by reflecting Tides of Blood with W and executing him with Golden Eclipse after his pool is spent.
edits.after: At 2+ items you win by blocking Tides of Blood with W and executing him with Golden Eclipse after his pool is spent.

edits.before: Two items in you punish his engage: W reflects his Tides of Blood, Golden Eclipse (R) executes him as his pool comes off cooldown, and his Hemoplague amp can't save him if you catch him post-pool. Bait Sanguine Pool (W) then E-lock him.
edits.after: Two items in you punish his engage: W blocks his Tides of Blood, Golden Eclipse (R) executes him as his pool comes off cooldown, and his Hemoplague amp can't save him if you catch him post-pool. Bait Sanguine Pool (W) then E-lock him.

edits.before: After items you retake control: your Q out-paces his sustain, Rebuttal (W) reflects Tides of Blood, and Golden Eclipse (R) executes him once his pool is spent. Bait Sanguine Pool (W), lock Solar Snare (E) on the recovery frames, and his healing can't save him.
edits.after: After items you retake control: your Q out-paces his sustain, Rebuttal (W) blocks Tides of Blood, and Golden Eclipse (R) executes him once his pool is spent. Bait Sanguine Pool (W), lock Solar Snare (E) on the recovery frames, and his healing can't save him.

notes: Chart rows 5 (First item) and 6 (2+ items) still disagree across layers: full says Vladimir, content and packet levelChart say Mel, and the packet flags the chart as contradicting the 43.98% win rate (which favours Vladimir overall). I could not settle it from the kits alone, so per the chart rule I left both rows untouched — pre-existing disagreement, not newly introduced. packet suspectNames flagged 'Use Sanguine Pool' in wants.foe[1] but that is the correct ability name — false positive, no edit. Changed 'reflects Tides of Blood' to 'blocks' throughout: E carries no projectile flag (self-AoE), though Mel W does prevent the damage while active.
